findings.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — Denial cache is checked before identity resolution, and its key uses raw checkReq.UserUID while the permission cache key uses resolved userIdentifiers.UID; inconsistent keys can produce wrong deny decisions or useless entries

[High/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:158 — Denial cache entries are never invalidated when permissions change; a newly granted permission is still denied for up to shortCacheTTL because cached denial is consulted before the fresh permission cache

[Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:120-137 — When cached permissions exist but the check is denied, the code falls through to a full getIdentityPermissions DB fetch on every such request, defeating the permission cache; cache the denial from cached-perm evaluation instead

[Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey uses '_' as separator with user-supplied values (userUID, action, name, parent), allowing key collisions; use an unambiguous encoding like colon-joined or hashed keys

[Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:158 — Denial is cached whenever checkPermission returns false, but deny may stem from transient/incomplete state (e.g. missing team membership, silent folder resolution failures); cache hard denials only for authoritative denies

[Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:124 — Errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are silently swallowed by the if err == nil pattern, including GetUserIdentifiers errors and the unsupported identity type error; log or short-circuit instead of treating as benign cache miss

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go — No test covers the 'cached permissions exist but check is denied' path (DB-fallthrough + denial-cache-set, lines 130-136), nor asserts a denial cache entry is written on deny

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:377-420 — Removing cache read and permissionCacheUsage metrics from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions means external callers no longer record cache-hit metrics, and the false cache-usage counter in Check increments even when singleflight-cached results are served, making metrics misleading
[Low/doc_defect] pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:101 — NoopCache for the in-process client is undocumented; add a comment explaining why the noop cache is explicitly passed to avoid confusion

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — Denial cache is checked before identity resolution, and its key uses raw checkReq.UserUID while the permission cache key uses resolved userIdentifiers.UID; inconsistent keys can produce wrong deny decisions or useless entries

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the denial cache key is built and checked using `checkReq.UserUID` before calling `GetUserIdentifiers` (`permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.UserUID, ...)`), while the permission cache keys for users/service accounts are built using the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID` in `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (`userPermCacheKey(ns.Value, userIdentifiers.UID, action)`). This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency that could reduce cache effectiveness or cause misses if `checkReq.UserUID` is not already the canonical UID, though the diff alone doesn’t prove it will cause incorrect deny decisions in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:158 — Denial cache entries are never invalidated when permissions change; a newly granted permission is still denied for up to shortCacheTTL because cached denial is consulted before the fresh permission cache

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new permDenialCache is consulted first and causes an immediate deny if a key exists (lines added around permDenialKey/Get). That denial entry is only ever added on a deny (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`) and is never cleared/invalidated on a subsequent allow, nor is it checked after permission evaluation. Therefore, if permissions change to allow (or permCache later contains an allow), a previously cached denial will still force denial until TTL expiry, because it short-circuits before permission cache/DB checks.

matched_golden_ids: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that when a cached-permissions check results in denial, the code ignores that outcome and falls through to a DB fetch each time, i.e., cached denials aren’t trusted/used. This matches the golden issue’s core point about asymmetric cache trust (trusting cached grants but not cached denials), though the candidate emphasizes cache inefficiency more than the security implication of stale cached grants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:158 — Denial is cached whenever checkPermission returns false, but deny may stem from transient/incomplete state (e.g. missing team membership, silent folder resolution failures); cache hard denials only for authoritative denies

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `permDenialCache` that is checked before any permission lookup: if the key exists, `Check` returns `Allowed: false` immediately (service.go:113-121). The cache is populated whenever `allowed` is false after the DB-backed permission fetch and `checkPermission` (service.go:150-153). This means a previously-denied check can be “sticky” for the cache TTL and will block re-evaluation even if underlying authorization state changes shortly after (e.g., permission grant/team membership update), because the denial cache short-circuits all other logic (including the DB fallback used to correct stale `permCache`). That is a concrete, behavior-changing correctness risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:124 — Errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are silently swallowed by the if err == nil pattern, including GetUserIdentifiers errors and the unsupported identity type error; log or short-circuit instead of treating as benign cache miss

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new cache fast-path does `cachedPerms, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions(...); if err == nil { ... }` and otherwise falls through to `s.getIdentityPermissions(...)`. This does ignore non-cache-miss errors from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (including `GetUserIdentifiers` failures and `unsupported identity type`), but those errors are not fully “silently swallowed”: the code will typically hit the same error again in `getIdentityPermissions` and then log/return it. The real diff-grounded issue is wasted work (double lookup) and miscounting `permissionCacheUsage` as a cache miss for non-ErrNotFound errors, rather than a correctness break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go — No test covers the 'cached permissions exist but check is denied' path (DB-fallthrough + denial-cache-set, lines 130-136), nor asserts a denial cache entry is written on deny

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in Service.Check to (a) fall through to DB when cached permissions exist but `checkPermission` returns `allowed == false` (lines around the new `getCachedIdentityPermissions` call), and (b) write to `permDenialCache` when the final decision is deny (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`). The new tests cover: allow from cached perms, DB fallback on cache miss, DB fallback when cached perms don’t include the requested item (outdated cache but DB allows), and deny when a denial cache entry already exists. There is no test for the path where cached permissions are present yet deny (triggering DB fallback) and the final result is still deny, nor any assertion that `permDenialCache` is written on deny.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:377-420 — Removing cache read and permissionCacheUsage metrics from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions means external callers no longer record cache-hit metrics, and the false cache-usage counter in Check increments even when singleflight-cached results are served, making metrics misleading

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the permCache read and associated permissionCacheUsage increments from getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions (service.go: getUserPermissions cache-hit path deleted; getAnonymousPermissions cache-hit check deleted). Cache usage is now tracked earlier in Check/List via getCachedIdentityPermissions. In Check, metrics.permissionCacheUsage is only incremented as a "true" hit when cachedPerms both exist and allow; if cachedPerms exist but don’t allow (outdated/incomplete) it falls through and increments the "false" counter (service.go:113-145), so the metric can undercount cache reads/usage and overcount misses. This is metrics semantics/observability accuracy, not a functional correctness defect. The claim about “external callers” can’t be verified from the diff (getUserPermissions is unexported and call sites aren’t fully shown), but the metrics-shift/misleading-count concern is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:101 — NoopCache for the in-process client is undocumented; add a comment explaining why the noop cache is explicitly passed to avoid confusion

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a new NoopCache passed to the in-process client (ProvideAuthZClient uses authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), and NoopCache is defined without any comment). However, the finding is purely a documentation/style request (add a comment to avoid confusion) rather than a verifiable defect or substantive review issue grounded in behavior.
